name: date-picker
description: Date input with a calendar dropdown — single dates or ranges (start and end fields, presets, two months), dates typed in the page's own format, a clear button, and an inline variant with the calendar always shown; the month grid is the nested `calendar` recipe

changes.note: Ranges, typing, clearing, inline. (1) data-mode="range" (on the picker; it is the nested calendar's mode too): an [data-part="input-end"] field beside [data-part="input"], with an optional [data-part="separator"], shows the end; [data-part="value-end"] is the hidden input that submits it, next to [data-part="value"] for the start. The popup is the calendar in range mode — presets, hover preview and the summary come with it — and a calendar with data-months="2" shows two months when the viewport is at least 48rem wide, one below that. A range is committed (popup closed, focus back on the input, faqir:date-change emitted) when its end is picked; a single input in range mode shows the whole range and is display-only. (2) Typing: a field without readonly reads what is typed on blur (change) and Enter, in the field order and month names of the nearest lang (Intl.DateTimeFormat formatToParts; navigator.language when no lang is set): 1–2 digit days and months, a month name, 2- or 4-digit years, any separators, and ISO YYYY-MM-DD or another year-first entry always. A real date inside min/max and not disabled is shown in full ("March 14, 2026"), stored and emitted; anything else keeps the text the person typed, gets aria-invalid="true" and data-state="invalid" (the field turns destructive), empties the submitted value, and shows an optional [data-part="error"]. A range checks that the end is not before the start and that the span respects the calendar's data-min-range/data-max-range. A typed field with no placeholder shows the page's pattern (mm/dd/yyyy, dd.mm.yyyy, yyyy/mm/dd). (3) [data-part="field"]: one input-styled box holding the field(s), the clear button and a [data-part="trigger"] icon button — the markup for typing and for ranges; the classic [data-part="trigger"] wrapper still works. (4) [data-part="clear"]: a button with an accessible name, hidden until there is something to clear; it empties every field and value, emits faqir:date-change with null dates, and returns focus to the input. (5) data-variant="inline": the calendar sits in the flow, always shown, with no popup, dialog role, aria-expanded or outside-click; picking a day fills the field without moving focus. open()/close() only flip data-state there, and the trigger slot is no longer required (it is for the popover). (6) Keyboard: ArrowDown (or Alt+ArrowDown) on a field opens the calendar and focuses the selected day — and Enter/Space on a read-only field — so a closed picker is reachable without a pointer; Escape closes as before. The combobox input now carries aria-controls naming the popup (axe aria-required-attr when expanded). (7) The display is formatted with Intl in the nearest lang; en-US output is unchanged ("October 15, 2026"). The decorative icon is the icon primitive (data-ui="icon" data-icon="calendar"), not an emoji. Existing markup, values and events behave as before.

A value part for forms. [data-part="value"] is an optional <input type="hidden"> directly inside the root that carries the field's name: the controller keeps the ISO date (2026-10-15) in it on every pick, setValue() and clear, and fires input and change on it so l-model, faqir-validate and faqir-rules see the answer. The visible [data-part="input"] keeps the display text ("October 15, 2026") and loses its name, so FormData and a native submit send the ISO date instead of the display text. A value rendered into the hidden input is the picker's selection at start-up, and a form reset restores it. A new clear() method empties the calendar, the visible input and the value part (setValue still ignores anything that is not a date). Markup without the value part behaves exactly as before.

Nested components keep their own parts. The stylesheet reached the trigger, input, icon and calendar with descendant selectors, so a component nested inside with parts of the same name took this one's styles. Parts are root > trigger > input and icon, and root > calendar. Every part rule is now a child chain from the root, with the hops in :where(), so no rule changes specificity. No change for markup that follows the template.

BREAKING: the month grid moves out into the standalone calendar recipe (task 0.4-10). Seven parts date-picker declared and styled in 1.x now belong to calendar and are gone from this manifest and this stylesheet: data-part="header", data-part="nav-prev", data-part="nav-next", data-part="month-label", data-part="grid", data-part="grid-body" and data-part="day", together with the day cell's markers data-date, data-today="true" and data-outside="true". Migration is two steps: run `faqir add calendar` (date-picker no longer carries the grid's CSS, so without it the month grid renders unstyled), then wrap the grid markup inside [data-part="calendar"] in a <div data-ui="calendar"> root. Behaviour survives either way — the controller falls back to treating the popup itself as the calendar root when no [data-ui="calendar"] is nested — so an unmigrated page keeps working and loses only its styling and its audit. This entry is the record 1.1.0 shipped without: the extraction was a minor bump with no changelog at all, which is what the v0.2.4 → 1.0 surface gate now makes impossible.

value.description: Inside a form: an <input type="hidden"> directly inside the root, carrying the field's name. The controller keeps the ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) in it and fires input/change on it whenever the value changes, so it is what FormData, a native submit, l-model and the rules read. The visible input then carries no name.

value-end.description: Range mode in a form: a second <input type="hidden"> directly inside the root, carrying the end's name and ISO date (value carries the start). Same input/change events as value

trigger.description: What opens the calendar: the classic clickable wrapper around input and icon, or — inside field — a <button> with an aria-label ("Open calendar"). Optional for the inline variant. Required for the popover; the inline variant has none

field.description: One input-styled box holding the field(s), an optional separator, clear and an icon-button trigger — the markup for typed dates and for ranges. The focus ring and the invalid border are drawn on it

input.description: Text input displaying the selected date as a person reads it ("October 15, 2026") — the start in range mode. readonly: a click (or Enter/Space/ArrowDown) opens the calendar; without readonly a typed date is read on blur and Enter. Inside a form it carries the label's id, required and the description wiring but no name — the value part is what submits

separator.description: Range: the decorative mark between the start and end fields (aria-hidden)

input-end.description: Range mode: the end date's field, a sibling of input inside field. Read-only opens the calendar; without readonly it is typed like input. Give it role="combobox" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" to open the popup from it too

clear.description: A button with an aria-label ("Clear date") inside field or trigger, hidden by the controller until a field has text. Empties the fields and the value parts, emits faqir:date-change with null dates, and returns focus to input

icon.description: Decorative calendar glyph inside the classic trigger (aria-hidden) — the icon primitive, data-ui="icon" data-icon="calendar"

error.description: Optional message directly inside the root, shown while a typed field is invalid (start it hidden). Point the field's aria-errormessage at its id

calendar.description: Calendar container: a role="dialog" popup with an aria-label, or for the inline variant a plain block in the flow. Canonically nests a [data-ui='calendar'] recipe that owns the header, month navigation, presets and day grid; legacy markup with those parts placed directly inside this container keeps working

invalid.description: On a typed field (input or input-end) whose text is not a valid date — also aria-invalid="true". The text stays as typed; the field's box is drawn in the destructive colour

methods.name: setValue
methods.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or for a range "start,end" / { start, end }; anything that is not a date is ignored.

value.description: Selected date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD: the value part's value (and the visible input's data-value). Range: value holds the start and value-end the end; setValue takes "start,end" or { start, end }

mode.description: data-mode: one date, or a start and an end (input + input-end, value + value-end); passed to the nested calendar

required_attrs: aria-expanded and aria-controls on the combobox input(s), kept by the controller unless inline
role="dialog" and aria-label on the calendar container unless inline
role="grid" on the nested calendar grid
aria-label on day buttons with full date
aria-label on clear and on a trigger button
aria-invalid="true" on a typed field when its text is not a valid date (aria-errormessage may point at error)

keyboard.Escape: close calendar, focus returns to the input
keyboard.ArrowDown / Alt+ArrowDown (field): open the calendar and focus the selected day
keyboard.Enter (typed field): read the typed date and show it in full (the form still submits)
keyboard.Tab (typed field): leaving the field reads the typed date
keyboard.Enter/Space: select focused day (range: start, then end)
keyboard.Home: focus first day of the week
keyboard.End: focus last day of the week
